Apple CEO Tim Cook today announced that Apple will donate to support relief efforts following the devastating earthquake in Indonesia. Details below.

Apple to donate in support of Indonesia earthquake relief efforts

Over the past few years, Apple has consistently donated in response to major earthquakes, floods, and other emergencies around the world to assist relief efforts.

In just the past two months, the company has already supported relief efforts in Venezuela, Southern Europe, and Japan. Following the magnitude 7.7 earthquake in Indonesia over the weekend, Tim Cook announced today that Apple will also donate to support local relief work.

As is customary, Cook did not disclose the amount of Apple's donation nor specify which organisations would receive the funds.

9to5Mac Take

Beyond donating in response to natural disasters and other emergencies, Apple also operates an internal giving programme called "Employee Giving." Through the company's donation matching policy, it has raised over US$880 million to date.

Since Tim Cook announced his decision to step down as Apple CEO, discussions about his legacy have never ceased. Apple's commitment to charitable and humanitarian work has been a significant part of his tenure, and it is hoped that this spirit will continue under John Ternus's leadership.
